root_idea.summary: The root centers on sending or extending something downward or outward, and on an extended route or course.
root_idea.development: The downward-extension idea appears in hanging garments, falling rain, flowing hair, and vessel edges; extension in length develops into سَبِيلٌ, a way or path, and related travel and grain-ear usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quranic group is the noun سَبِيلٌ and is displayed under its normalized dictionary headword.

senses.definition: A way, road, path, or route; a traversable course.
senses.usage_conditions: Used literally for a road or route and, in the plural سُبُلٌ, for ways or paths. The term can also denote a clear, open, or easy route.

senses.definition: A course, way, or cause of action, whether good or evil; especially the way of God, religion, truth, guidance, or righteous action.
senses.usage_conditions: Common in expressions such as سَبِيلُ اللَّهِ, سَبِيلُ رَبِّكَ, سُبُلُ السَّلَامِ, and related constructions. In religious usage it may refer to the cause or way by which one seeks divine favor, and it is often associated with striving or good works.

senses.definition: A means of access, connection, or approach to an end; an avenue to safety or salvation.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative use for a means by which one reaches something, including a way to safety or Paradise. It is attested in the construction of taking or finding a سَبِيلٌ with or toward someone or something.

senses.definition: A wayfarer or traveler, especially one stranded away from home, in the expression ابنُ السَّبِيلِ.
senses.usage_conditions: The phrase literally presents the traveler as the “son of the road.” Quranic usage includes a traveler whose journey or access to resources has been cut off, and who therefore requires assistance.

senses.definition: A ground for blame, reproach, or liability.
senses.usage_conditions: In constructions such as ما عَلَى ... مِنْ سَبِيلٍ, it denotes no basis for blame or liability; in إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى ..., it denotes the liability or blame that does apply.

senses.definition: In the Quranic construction تَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ, to cut off or obstruct the way.
senses.usage_conditions: The passage is interpreted either as preventing offspring through unnatural sexual conduct or as confronting travelers on the roads for an obscene purpose. These are interpretations of the cited construction, not general restrictions on the noun سَبِيلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dedicate property, its revenue, or its usufruct to charitable, religious, or other pious uses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used of assigning an estate or its profits to the way of God, wayfarers, the poor, or fighters; also of making benefits freely available to designated beneficiaries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or become long in the سَبَلَة, especially the beard or hanging facial hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived use connected with the length or hanging of the beard or moustache.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a road, to have travelers following or passing along it repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a road with successive or recurring movement of people upon it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To let down, lower, or make something hang down or trail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a waist-wrapper, garment, veil, curtain, skirt, tail, or a part of the beard; the intransitive use describes something falling or hanging upon the breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour, shed, or fall abundantly or continuously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water, rain, tears, and flowing blood; it can also describe speech poured forth profusely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a crop, to put forth ears or grain-heads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is also related by cross-reference to سَنْبَلَ and تَسَنْبَلَ in this agricultural sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something let loose, let down, made to hang, or made to trail; especially hanging or trailing garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote what has been allowed to hang down or garments made to drag on the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain, including rain issuing from clouds, flowing rain, or flowing blood by extension.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from something descending or flowing from above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a particular excellent mare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name use reported as belonging to a specific mare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name used for a ewe or she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A naming or calling use, including the call used when asking the animal to be milked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ear or head of grain, or the spreading awns or extremities of a grain ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer especially to a bending or inclining ear and is used alongside سُنْبُلٌ and سَبُولَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Virgo, or the star Spica in Virgo.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical and astrological proper-name use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant associated with Indian spikenard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant-name wording is transmitted in the discussion of the grain-ear terminology and is retained as a cautious lexical identification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper edges, lips, or head of a vessel, especially a bucket or drinking vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of filling a vessel up to its edges or lips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A number of spears, few or many.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended use associated with the heads of spears and grain ears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in an imprecation concerning making the nose cleave to the ground, figuratively abasing or humbling someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coarse garment made from the hard or hurds of flax.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized textile use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or film of the eye resembling a web, with visible red veins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical ophthalmic term for a film or covering over the eye, associated by analogy with a lowered veil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reviling or vilification between people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression that there is سَبَلٌ between two persons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long and flaccid, specifically of the scrotum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing length and laxity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain covering a wide extent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized rain term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The moustache or beard, especially the hair hanging from the front of the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is variously applied to the moustache, its extremity, the forepart of the beard, or the hair hanging toward the breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper breast region of a camel, or the hair or skin on that region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the place where a camel is stabbed or struck above the breast, and of its associated hair or skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A public drinking fountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later usage of the noun, distinct from its Quranic senses of way or course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A traveler, or a company of travelers, moving along a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective use can denote people following or succeeding one another on roads to accomplish their needs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A traveled or beaten road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually occurs in the expression سَبِيلٌ سَابِلَةٌ or an equivalent description of a road used by traffic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain falling continuously, in successive showers, in large drops, or copiously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use derived from repeated falling or flowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a fountain in Paradise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Quranic proper name, not a form of the public headword سَبِيلٌ; the reported Lane citation uses its historical Quran-reference convention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having long or hanging hair, including a long beard, moustache hair, or eyelashes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form can describe a woman with hair in the moustache area; the adjective can also describe an eye with long lashes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who lengthens a garment and lets it hang or trail to the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman according to the garment being made to hang down.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The penis, by reference to its pendulousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lizard called ضَبّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical name reported in the classical vocabulary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow used in the game of maysir, identified as the fifth or, according to another report, the sixth arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The arrow is also called المُصْفَحُ and is described as having six notches and six assigned shares or fines.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the month of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A calendrical name associated in the report with the time of ʿĀd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ugly old man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is explained as possibly referring to the length of his beard.

cautions: The public Quranic form is normalized to the dictionary citation form سَبِيلٌ; inflection, definiteness, attached pronouns, and the plural سُبُلٌ are not separate public forms.
سَلْسَبِيلُ is retained as a distinct lexical proper name rather than merged into the Quranic form سَبِيلٌ.

Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation conventions. The interpretation associated with its citation of the access sense is preserved without inventing a modern verse location not securely supplied for that occurrence.
The plant-name wording in the classical grain-ear discussion is textually compressed and is therefore presented cautiously.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane plant reference within lane-unit:sbl:40134:g2:main does not identify its precise headword unambiguously; it is assigned cautiously to a spikenard-related classical entry rather than treated as a Quranic form.
